title: Rollout Swap Scorecard and Fast-Rollback Prototype
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: engineering teams need a fast, confident way to recover from a bad canary or A/B variant without increasing cognitive load or introducing unsafe shortcuts. Prior designs focus on gradual traffic sculpting; incidents show teams sometimes need a one-click emergency swap but also want clear evidence of risk and auditability.

Goals: 1) Surface a lightweight Rollout Confidence Scorecard that synthesizes key signals (latency, error rate, model quality regressions, cost delta) for each variant so a dev can make a fast call. 2) Provide an Emergency Swap (fast-rollback) UX that: preserves auditability, enforces RBAC and two-step confirmations for high-risk orgs, and optionally runs a dry-run simulation. 3) Keep the main rollout composer uncluttered while making the swap path discoverable and safe.

Scope: design the Scorecard card (summary + expand for time series), the Emergency Swap flow (confirmations, optional simulation, immediate revert), and the small Rollout Swap animation/state transitions in the console. Handoff-ready Figma prototype and component spec required.
design_notes:
Scorecard should calculate a single confidence score (0-100) with breakdowns. Primary signals: 95th latency, HTTP/GRPC error rate, semantic quality regressions from eval harness, unmatched user intent fraction, and token cost per request. Use a red/amber/green band with clear CTA affordances. Emergency Swap should be visually distinct from routine 'increase traffic' actions: put as a contextual action on the active rollout header and behind a color-coded guard. Consider adding optional 'swap with shadowing' mode: route all traffic to new variant but keep old variant in shadow mode for comparison.

Trade-offs discussed: 1) Immediate swap reduces time-to-recovery but risks data drift; mitigation: allow instant swap plus automatic scheduled rollback if post-swap quality degrades beyond thresholds. 2) Too many confirmations slow down response; mitigation: org-level policy to allow single-click for owners and require 2-step for others. 3) Surface of scorecard must be explainable to non-ML engineers; provide short hover tips and link to evaluation artifacts.
updates: 2025-11-02: Kickoff with PM and SRE. Confirm signals to surface: p95 latency, 5xx rate, model-answer-regression (from evals), token-cost change, and user-affect metric (click-through on ML features).

2025-11-04: Wireframes v1 completed. Chose a compact horizontal scorecard with expand-to-detail micro interaction. Decision: confidence score normalized across signals using weighted sum controlled by PM. Open question: weights default vs team overrides.

2025-11-05: Design review with Research. Research requested a quick usability test focusing on emergency mental models; scheduled moderated sessions with 6 platform engineers (target date 2025-11-10).

2025-11-06: Incorporated feedback from Security on audit trail requirements: include an explicit forced-comment step option and a visual audit token attached to the swap action. Added RBAC callouts to flows.

2025-11-07: High-fidelity prototype assembled. Animation for swap transition (traffic dial morph) added. Noted performance implications: frontend must poll rollout metrics at low latency; engineering to estimate additional streaming subscription cost (ENG-23045).

2025-11-08: Paired with backend engineer to add a 'dry-run' API wire: /rollouts/:id/swap-simulate. PM suggested a delayed automatic re-eval 5 minutes post-swap to trigger auto-rollback if signals drop below safety thresholds. Added to dependencies.

2025-11-09: Internal design critique. Feedback: simplify confirmation modal copy, clarify difference between Swap and Revert, add microcopy explaining simulated swap vs live swap. Preparing final handoff artifacts and component tokens.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive Figma prototype (desktop) with: scorecard collapsed and expanded states, emergency swap flow, confirmation modal, and revert path
Component spec with tokens, spacing, color states, and accessibility notes (contrast, keyboard flow)
Handoff doc with API contract examples for ENG: swap (immediate), swap-simulate (dry-run), swap-revert
Usability test report with 6 platform engineers showing median task time <= 90s to complete emergency swap and no major errors
Design review sign-off from PM (Harper Li) and SRE lead (Jordan Kim)
usability_testing: Metrics: task completion time, confidence rating (1-5), error rate
engineering_handoff: GitHub PR template added in PR 412 for backend work
qa_notes: QA should validate telemetry tags for swap events (swap.initiated, swap.confirmed, swap.reverted)
Confirm audit comments are persisted and visible in rollout timeline
Verify RBAC prevents non-owner from executing fast-swap when org policy requires 2-step confirmation
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: accidental swap by junior engineer - Mitigation: org-level policy and sticky confirmation for first swap in 24h
Risk: metrics lag causing bad decision - Mitigation: surface metric freshness and last-updated timestamp on scorecard
Risk: unexpected cost spike - Mitigation: show estimated token-cost delta on scorecard and add optional cost-cap guard
